name: beats: after a comma, "so" opens a sentence of its own whatever its subject ("..., so undoing a subtraction means ..."), except in "so that", "so as to" and "so far as", which stay whole; a sentence under the limit is not cut even where it could be

sentences.the judge's 8.2 s: The rule here is that whatever you do to one side, you do to the other, so undoing a subtraction means adding the same amount to both sides.
sentences.the judge's 8.0 s: When a term moves from one side of the equals sign to the other you are really doing something to both sides, so moving a term across means undoing it with the opposite operation.
sentences.so that: You add the same amount to both sides of the equation every single time, so that the two sides stay equal and the answer does not change.
sentences.so as to: You move every term with x to the left side of the equals sign first, so as to have the plain numbers alone on the right.
sentences.so far as: Nothing on the page says which of the two files is loaded first when the app starts, so far as the lines I can read go.
sentences.20 words, under the limit: That Map resets on every restart and isn't shared between server instances, so limits leak on serverless or multiple processes.
